questions.question_text:
In a class of 30, the ratio of girls to boys is $2:3$.
How many boys are in the class?

options.why: Calculated $30\div3=10$, dividing the total by the boys' ratio number instead of dividing by all $5$ parts and then multiplying by $3$.
Uses the ratio number without scaling it to a total of 30.
Splits the class into two equal groups instead of five ratio parts.

questions.solution_text: There are $2+3=5$ equal parts, so each part is $30/5=6$. Boys make up three parts: $3\times6=18$.

questions.question_text:
Adam and Matt share $\$91$ in the ratio $2:5$.
How much does each person receive?

options.why: Calculated the shares correctly but assigned the $5$ parts to Adam and the $2$ parts to Matt.
Calculated $\$91\div2=\$45.50$ for each person, ignoring the ratio.
Calculated $\$91\div5=\$18.20$ as the value of $1$ part, then multiplied by $2$ and $5$, using Matt's parts instead of the total $7$ parts.

questions.solution_text:
$2+5=7\text{ parts}$
$7\text{ parts}=\$91$
$1\text{ part}=\$13$
$2\text{ parts}=\$26$
$5\text{ parts}=\$65$
Adam receives $\$26$ and Matt receives $\$65$.
